headlines.title: How Is NVIDIA Expanding AI-Powered Telecom Networks Following T-Mobile’s First AI-RAN Call?
headlines.summary: What did T-Mobile and NVIDIA announce at GTC Berlin?NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) announced at its GTC Berlin event that T-Mobile US (NASDAQ:TMUS) had completed what the companies described as the world’s first AI Radio Access Network (AI-RAN) call on a commercial mobile network. The demonstration took place in Bellevue, Washington, in collaboration with NVIDIA and Nokia (NYSE:NOK).

headlines.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang Sees 100GW AI Opportunity In Telecom Networks, With TMUS, NOK Already Making Moves
headlines.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang cited about 100,000 sites and 100 gigawatts of distributed data center capacity in outlining the potential scale of the opportunity.

headlines.title: T-Mobile and First Responders Children’s Foundation Celebrate National First Responders Day Nationwide
headlines.summary: NEW YORK, October 21, 2026--T-Mobile and First Responders Children’s Foundation (FRCF) are putting the spotlight on the heroes who serve our communities every day. The celebration kicks off October 24 with first responder appreciation events at 25 T-Mobile stores nationwide, followed by the First Responders Children’s Foundation 2026 Roll Call of Heroes ceremony in Times Square on October 28, hosted by Jon Stewart.

headlines.title: T-Mobile (TMUS): Can Fiber Grow Without Consuming Too Much Shareholder Cash?
headlines.summary: T-Mobile US, Inc. (NASDAQ:TMUS) wants fiber to deepen relationships with wireless households while partners help finance and operate the networks. Across telecom services stocks, bundling mobile and home internet creates another recurring bill per customer. That strengthens the investment case when retention and service margins repay expansion costs. T-Mobile US, Inc.

headlines.title: AT&T Sinks 5% Despite Q3 Beat and Raised Outlook; Verizon and T-Mobile Drop 3%
headlines.summary: AT&T just posted a quarter that beat forecasts and lifted its profit outlook, yet its stock is getting punished harder than those of its two biggest rivals. A non-cash write-down, a satellite company circling the wireless market, and a fiber bet that may or may not hold explain why investors are not impressed.

description: T-Mobile US, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, provides wireless communications services in the United States, Puerto Rico, and the United States Virgin Islands. The company offers voice, messaging, and data services to postpaid, prepaid, and wholesale and other services customers. It also provides wireless devices, including smartphones, wearables, tablets, home broadband gateways, headsets, and other mobile communication devices, as well as accessories; financing through equipment installment plans; reinsurance for device insurance policies and extended warranty contracts. The company offers services under the T-Mobile, Metro by T-Mobile, and Mint Mobile brands through its owned and operated retail stores, customer care channels, national retailers, and its websites, as well as through T-Mobile, Metro by T-Mobile, and Mint Mobile apps. It also sells devices to dealers and other third-party distributors for resale through independent third-party retail outlets and various third-party websites. It has 700 MHz wireless spectrum licenses. The company was founded in 1994 and is headquartered in Bellevue, Washington. T-Mobile US, Inc. operates as a subsidiary of Deutsche Telekom AG.
